issue_context.title: Introduce JSON logging format for kube-proxy
issue_context.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

Structured logging support in k8s allows specifying logging in JSON. Many k8s components like apiServer, scheduler have support for json. This issue tracks adding JSON logging support for kube-proxy.  

#### Breakdown of the task

To get json logging support, changes have to be made in kube-proxy and Kind e2e script (for Prow/CI runs) which uses KubeProxyConfiguration 

1. Introduce logging-format (--logging-format string  ) option in kube-proxy. Currently there is none. ([link](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kube-proxy/))
2. Introduce an option in [KubeProxyConfiguration](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-proxy/blob/v0.22.1/config/v1alpha1/types.go#L104) so that kubeadm/kind can specify logging-format. Whether this "configuration option" is something generic or specific to logging needs input from a kube-proxy domain expert.
3. Update Kind to make use of the above 2 and specify the logging format similar to how we do for control-plane components. 
4. Prow/test-infra CI runs will have json logging enabled for kube-proxy.

#### Why is this needed:
To get the benefits of structured logging.

/sig network
/cc @serathius 
/cc @BenTheElder

I suspect that encoding as string is a potentially breaking change:
some tool might use this API to generate configuration files for Kubernetes 1.27. Once that tool gets updated, it writes a config that 1.27 cannot parse.

This is completely hypothetical. I am not aware of any such tool.

A safer alternative would be to encode as integer. As long as no-one ever develops a tool that writes configs, it won't make a difference. But if someone does, it'll be annoying that the result is not as human-friendly as a string.

@liggitt ?
I'd tend to favor the clear / human-friendly option... if there was such a tool it could use the 1.27 API definition until it no longer needed to support 1.27 schedulers
So do we need any changes here?
No. Let's go with "human friendly" (= current code).

Aren't all command line flags already deprecated in favor of the config fields?

```console
$ go run ./cmd/kube-proxy --logging-format=json
I0510 15:26:19.269444   67867 server.go:235] "Warning, all flags other than --config, --write-config-to, and --cleanup are deprecated, please begin using a config file ASAP"
I0510 15:26:19.269491   67867 server_others.go:75] "Using iptables proxy"
{"ts":1683725179269.8264,"caller":"app/server.go:538","msg":"Neither kubeconfig file nor master URL was specified, falling back to in-cluster config","v":0}
{"ts":1683725179269.8413,"caller":"app/server.go:491","msg":"Error running ProxyServer","err":"unable to load in-cluster configuration, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST and KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT must be defined"}
{"ts":1683725179269.864,"caller":"cli/run.go:74","msg":"command failed","err":"unable to load in-cluster configuration, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST and KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT must be defined"}
exit status 1
```

With that in mind, does it make sense to register these flags?

Another observation: ideally, the code which runs before `ValidateAndApplyAsField` shouldn't log anything because the desired logging configuration is still unknown. That's why we have a mixture of text and JSON log output here.

We've been kind of terrible about actually deprecating the command-line options in favor of config files, but yes, you're right, we should say that if people want to use the cool new features, they have to use the config file

On the other hand, these flags are the same that also other commands have. For the sake of consistency it would be nice if they were supported also in kube-proxy, not just the config options.

But then the warning needs to be modified so that it doesn't trigger for the logging parameters.

In the latest changes, I kept the logging-format flag and modified the warning, making sure the code which runs before ValidateAndApplyAsField shouldn't log anything.

Please review the changes, Thanks.
